overall_summary: Space-related anomalies and extreme cosmic paradoxes are currently driving the highest engagement and viewership on the channel, led by 'The Planet of Burning Ice' (1,053 views). Conversely, repetitive psychology and brain-related topics are underperforming, particularly when concepts are duplicated or re-uploaded within a short timeframe.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice Will Break Your Brain!' generated 1,053 views and 8 likes, while 'The Largest Ocean in Space' achieved 460 views.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on mind-bending space phenomena that present physical contradictions (e.g., dark stars, freezing planets, or liquid metal rain).

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Sharks Are Older Than Trees?' reached 302 views, and 'This Animal Literally Dies Every Winter!' reached 179 views.
winning_patterns.action: Produce content focusing on evolutionary timeline shocks and extreme biological survival mechanisms.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' generated only 5 views on its first upload and 54 views on the second. 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' got only 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: Pause generic brain-hack topics and pivot toward highly specific, newly discovered neurological anomalies.

weak_patterns.evidence: Re-uploading 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' within 2 days saw views drop from 183 to 118 with zero engagement on the second run.
weak_patterns.action: Implement a strict 30-day buffer before recycling any concept, ensuring a fresh script and visual hook are used.

experiment: Test a 'Timeline Shock' history format (e.g., 'Cleopatra lived closer to the iPhone than the building of the Great Pyramid') to see if historical scale paradoxes can match the high performance of cosmic paradoxes.
